anatomy.name: Root
anatomy.notes: The accordion container. It has no ARIA role; the items carry the semantics.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.action: Toggles the item open or closed (calls onOpenChange when open is controlled).

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.notes: Names the trigger (aria-labelledby) and the panel.

anatomy.name: Meta
anatomy.notes: The trigger's description (aria-describedby): screen readers read it after the name. Rendered from the subtitle prop. Same role and name as the cards' Meta; there it is an Inline of Duration and Certified, here a single Text.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.notes: chevron-down when closed, chevron-up when open. aria-hidden, so a virtual cursor does not read the glyph; the button name comes from aria-labelledby.

anatomy.name: PanelOuter
anatomy.notes: Grid wrapper whose row animates between 0fr and 1fr, so the height transition needs no measured height.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.notes: role=group, named by the title through aria-labelledby. While closed: hidden=until-found (find-in-page can reach and open it), or inert + aria-hidden where the browser lacks it.

figma.note: Text property on the Title layer.
Optional prop ↔ Has <x> boolean plus a text property on the Meta layer (ADR-023 amendment 2026-10-12). The property follows the prop and the layer follows the part (ADR-023 amendment 2026-11-19).

constraints.reason: Never pass both: AccordionItemProps makes it a type error, and at runtime the controlled open prop wins (a DEV-only warning fires). Use open + onOpenChange for controlled, or defaultOpen alone for uncontrolled.

states.name: hover
states.notes: Title and Indicator turn text.interactive.default; the trigger has no fill. Applies in both open and closed items.

states.name: active
states.notes: Momentary press feedback on the trigger (CSS :active): Title and Indicator turn text.interactive.hover, one step past hover; orthogonal to open/closed.

states.name: focus-visible
states.notes: No component rule: the global ring in styles/reset.css applies to the trigger (ADR-028), color.border.focus at size.focus.width, offset size.focus.offset.

states.name: closed
states.notes: Panel collapsed but still in the DOM, hidden with hidden=until-found (inert + aria-hidden in browsers without it): Tab skips its focusable content (FocusableContent story) and find-in-page opens it. Trigger shows chevron-down.

states.name: open
states.trigger: open true, or the item toggled while uncontrolled (aria-expanded=true)
states.notes: Panel visible on the item's ambient surface (no fill of its own); trigger shows chevron-up.

accessibility.notes: Each AccordionItem trigger is a <button> wrapped in a heading element (default h3, configurable via headingLevel). The button is named by the title alone (aria-labelledby); the subtitle is its description (aria-describedby), so a reader hears "Module 1, button, collapsed" and then "2 hours" after a pause, not the title three times with the subtitle. The panel is role=group (React Aria's DisclosurePanel default), also labelled by the title; group is not a landmark, so open panels don't crowd landmark navigation. The Accordion container itself has no ARIA role — it is a plain div. The chevron Icon inside each trigger carries aria-hidden="true" so browse-mode reading skips the glyph; the button name comes from aria-labelledby, so the Icon never feeds it. A collapsed panel gets hidden=until-found once its closing transition ends (inert covers it while it animates, because inert content is skipped by find-in-page). Find-in-page and text-fragment links fire beforematch on it, which opens the item: an uncontrolled item opens itself, a controlled one calls onOpenChange(true), and if it stays closed hidden=until-found is put back a frame later (the browser removes the attribute after beforematch). Browsers without beforematch keep inert + aria-hidden, and find-in-page can't reach collapsed text there. Focus on close: if an item closes while focus is inside its panel (a controlled close from panel content), focus moves to its trigger before the panel turns inert; otherwise focus would fall to <body>. A click or key on the trigger already leaves focus there.
ariaAttributes: aria-controls (trigger → panel id) — the panel stays in the DOM while collapsed, never conditionally rendered, so this id always resolves
aria-labelledby (trigger → title id, panel → title id)
aria-describedby (trigger → subtitle id, only when subtitle is set)
hidden='until-found' on the panel while collapsed, set after the height transition ends; where beforematch is unsupported, aria-hidden='true' and the inert DOM property instead

keyboardInteractions.action: Toggles the focused accordion item open or closed
Toggles the focused accordion item open or closed

Moves focus sequentially through any focusable content within an open panel, then to the next accordion trigger. Focusable descendants inside a collapsed panel are skipped — hidden=until-found doesn't render them (inert where the browser lacks it), so Tab cannot land on them even though they remain in the DOM for aria-controls.
The reverse of Tab; also skips focusable content inside collapsed panels.

color.reason: Inherits the parent element's text style.

sets.name: AccordionItem
sets.covers: One item: Open × State (6 variants), with Title, Has subtitle and Subtitle properties

sets.name: course-module-list example
sets.covers: The course-module-list example frame (not a component); items stacked from instances of the set

divergences.what: Figma has no Root: the AccordionItem set is a single item, and an accordion is items stacked in a frame (or the Accordion list set, which is the course-module-list pattern with Show more).
divergences.decision: Accepted: Root only stacks items and draws the top border, so the example frame shows it without a component of its own.
divergences.notes: The set was named Accordion until 2026-11-19 and renamed to match the code export. A Root component is tracked in #182.

divergences.what: Heading has no layer in Figma; Trigger sits directly in the item.
divergences.decision: Accepted: Heading is only the h3 element (headingLevel) around the button and draws nothing, so a wrapper layer would add nesting without anything to see or set.

divergences.what: PanelOuter and PanelInner exist only in code.
divergences.decision: Accepted: wrappers for the height animation, with no role a designer sets. The spec schema has no code-only marker for parts, so they are listed here.

divergences.what: The Panel holds a sample text layer in Figma; in code it takes any content (children).
divergences.decision: Accepted: designers show the panel's look, and real content is composed in code.
divergences.notes: A native slot (as CardVertical.Root's Body) was not added in the 2026-11-19 rebuild; revisit if designers need other content in the panel.

decisions.decision: The chevron colour is a token on the Indicator part, and the SVG paints it through `currentColor`. No colour prop or inline style is set on the Icon.
decisions.reason: A colour on the icon would bypass the colour tokens.
decisions.notes: Token: color.icon.default on .indicator in the CSS module. Applies the packages/components AGENTS.md Icon colour rule.

decisions.decision: A collapsed panel stays in the page, hidden with `hidden="until-found"` once it has finished closing, so find-in-page can still find its text and open it.
decisions.reason: `aria-controls` needs the panel to exist while collapsed, and find-in-page should still reach its text. Setting the attribute after the closing animation keeps the animation.
decisions.notes: Revised for #179 (2026-11-19). Earlier the panel was only inert + aria-hidden and the hidden attribute was rejected because display:none breaks the height transition. hidden=until-found applies content-visibility:hidden instead; it is set on Panel (inside PanelInner's overflow:hidden) after transitionend on PanelOuter, and inert covers the closing animation. Measured in Chromium 153: heights animate both ways; Tab skips collapsed content; real Cmd+F opened the item. Browsers without onbeforematch fall back to inert + aria-hidden. @types/react 18 types neither hidden=until-found nor onBeforeMatch, so both go through the ref. GOV.UK Frontend's accordion uses the same attribute and listener.

decisions.decision: If a controlled item does not open after find-in-page reveals it, the panel is hidden again a frame later.
decisions.reason: The browser unhides the panel itself. If your onOpenChange keeps the item closed, its links would otherwise become Tab stops you can't see.
decisions.notes: Adversarial review 2026-11-19 (medium): a declined beforematch left the panel without hidden or inert but still aria-hidden. index.tsx keeps isOpen in a ref and restores hidden=until-found in a requestAnimationFrame when still closed. The a11y test removes `hidden` after dispatching beforematch, as the browser does; a synthetic event alone can't catch this.

decisions.decision: The panel waits for its closing transition only when the browser reports one running (`getAnimations()`); otherwise it hides at once.
decisions.reason: No transition runs on mount, under a hidden ancestor, or when React Strict Mode re-runs effects. Waiting then would leave the panel inert, and find-in-page skips inert content.
decisions.notes: Adversarial review 2026-11-19 (low): a first-mount ref broke under StrictMode (showcase), leaving collapsed panels inert in dev. transitioncancel also triggers the hide. jsdom has no Web Animations API, so tests define getAnimations to simulate a running transition.

decisions.decision: When an item closes while focus is inside its panel, focus moves to the item's trigger.
decisions.reason: The closed panel becomes inert, which would drop focus to the top of the page and lose the reader's place.
decisions.notes: Done in the same layout effect that sets inert, before it is set. Covered by Accordion.a11y.test.tsx.

ruledOut.reason: Every open panel would be a landmark, and more than about six crowd the landmark list screen reader users navigate by.
ruledOut.notes: Was the role until 2026-11-19; replaced by group, React Aria DisclosurePanel's default.

ruledOut.option: Naming the trigger by its whole content (title and subtitle)
ruledOut.reason: Screen readers then read the title and subtitle as the heading, the button and the panel name, three times per item.

ruledOut.option: Panel right padding that clears the indicator column (calc of space.inset.md + size.icon.md + space.inline.sm)
ruledOut.reason: No Figma variable can hold a sum, so Figma kept a raw 48 that drifts if a token changes per device. Padding is now space.inset.md on both sides, and text can run under the indicator.
ruledOut.source: Figma binding check, 2026-11-20. Carbon caps line length with a percentage end padding instead; Spectrum deprecated its accordion-specific content padding tokens for semantic container padding.
ruledOut.notes: Added 2026-06-23 (36f9460) to keep panel text out from under the indicator. If that matters again, cap the line length with a max-width token (bindable in Figma) rather than a padding sum.
